notes: Channel decision: release convention (train.py/inference.py/benchmark.py/brazilband.py/array2h5.py all hardcode this): channel0001 is the SQUID readout, channel0002 is the injected reference/target. Probed median line-dominance was {'channel0001': 0.193, 'channel0002': 0.015}, inconclusive on its own and recorded for audit only; the release's own hardcoded convention is authoritative. Gate G0 (docs/results/TIDMAD_PHASE0_RESULT.md, evidence/tidmad/phase0/G0_baseline_reproduction.json): reproduced on the full 20-file validation set. `none` coarse score 1.1026 vs published 1.10 -- matches closely and is the calibration anchor for the whole contract (channel semantics, data integrity, environment). `savgol` coarse score -2.7708 vs published -2.35/-2.77 (coarse/fine) does NOT match to precision, but this is understood and non-blocking: the published hyperparameters (window_length=100, polyorder=11) sit in a numerically ill-conditioned regime for scipy's Vandermonde-based savgol_coeffs (coefficient sum collapses from ~1 to 1.7e-10 between polyorder 9 and 11), so the SG-filter baseline is not bit-reproducible by any implementation -- see the result doc for the coefficient-sum sweep. `injection_frequencies_by_file` replaces the earlier flat `injection_frequencies_hz` (now emptied, kept only as a legacy fallback field -- see TidmadDataContract.frequency_for_file) because TIDMAD's injected frequency is file- AND sample-range-specific, and a single flat value caused a real bug risk when more than one file was in play across phases 2/3/6 in the same session: abra_validation_0000.h5 (low-frequency band) = 69513.32 Hz, valid only for sample range [0, 2097152) -- that file's reference channel carries a persistent, genuine TWO-TONE signal at ~69510/69630 Hz (~120 Hz apart, comparable power, confirmed at nearly every 5-second-sampled timestamp across the full 190-second file via a 10-Hz-resolution FFT), a richer manifold than the single-frequency span{cos,sin} model Phase 3 assumes -- this is why Phase 3's real-mode rank test on file 0000 did not show the predicted rank-2 gain. abra_validation_0010.h5 (medium-high band) = 75000.0 Hz, valid only for sample range [0, 2097152) -- confirmed a clean single CW tone, but the reference-to-SQUID-channel coupling ratio there is only 0.057 (vs. 3.22 for file 0000): the calibration tone barely couples into the channel being reconstructed, which is why rank differences were not resolvable, not a reconstruction defect. abra_validation_0005.h5 (low-frequency band) = 8702.28 Hz, valid only for sample range [0, 2097152) -- selected by the predeclared file-selection rule in docs/results/TIDMAD_PREDECLARED_GATES.md (single-tone confirmed, prominence 2.59e7x median; observed-SQUID-channel SNR 3.42, first file in index order to pass both checks among 0001-0009/0011-0019). Coupling ratio (observed/reference amplitude) was found to fall off steeply and monotonically with frequency across the scanned files (7.13 at 5.7 kHz down to 0.0021 at 3.4 MHz), consistent with a low-pass-like transfer function between the reference/calibration channel and the SQUID readout -- a genuine physical property of the release worth noting, not particular to any one file. Do not reuse any of these frequencies for a different file or sample range without re-characterizing -- the injected frequency also sweeps slowly across each file's own 200-second duration (e.g. file 0010 sweeps ~75000 to ~89000 Hz over 190s, file 0015 sweeps ~620000 to ~760000 Hz).
